target_customer: Finance teams (CFOs, FP&A) at scale-ups and mid-market companies
problem: Finance teams plan and report in spreadsheets disconnected from operational data; Abacum pulls metrics from many systems into one collaborative planning, forecasting and reporting platform.

founders.name: Julio Martinez
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2021): fintech entrepreneur with an investment banking background.

founders.name: Jorge Lluch
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2021): former ESA engineer. Company copy calls both founders former CFOs; sources differ.

investors: angels incl. Justin Kan, Maximilian Tayenthal, Avi Meir

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs many finance-system integrations and a multi-dimensional modeling engine, standard but substantial SaaS engineering; SaaS launched June 2020 by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Once planning models and data connections live in the tool, switching is costly; but the category had many funded entrants, so no technical moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Abacum; it raised a Series B in June 2025 as an independent company.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (April 2021) framed legacy planning tools as old and spreadsheet-bound; early customers Typeform, Cabify and Ebury, over 50 customers by Nov 2021 per Fortune.

branding.domain_note: Used abacum.io early and abacum.ai later (the company site now serves abacum.ai); how the domains were acquired is not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise-credible with 'consumer-grade ease of use' positioning (company copy)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found; name resembles abacus and collides in search with unrelated Abacus companies.

outcome_analysis: Abacum launched in mid-2020, joined YC W21, raised a $7M seed (Apr 2021), a $25M Series A (Nov 2021) and a $60M Series B (Jun 2025). It is still independent. It grew in a crowded FP&A field by selling to scale-ups and mid-market finance teams, reportedly tripling revenue in the 12 months before the Series B with over half of revenue from the US. The long gap between rounds and the shift from Barcelona to New York headquarters are visible; the reasons are not given in sources.
notes: Seed and Series A each have a single outlet fetched plus other outlets seen in search listings (tech.eu, fintech.global). Series B reported as $60M (euro release says 52.5M); a 2026 date on a republished Axios item appears to be a republication. CB Insights shows about $92M total over 5 rounds versus 3 rounds recorded here, hence partial coverage. Company copy says over $100M raised. Series A date taken from Fortune article date. Name origin not found. No outcome search result for layoffs or shutdown.
